continuity_scope: Bounded to Djibril Tamsir Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali, translated by G. D. Pickett: the English published prose rendering attributed in its framing to Djeli Mamoudou Kouyaté of Djeliba Koro. This is a textualized, translation-specific witness, not a definitive text of a living Mande oral epic. Other jeli lineages, languages, performances, transcriptions, editions, and adaptations—including Jeli Fa-Digi Sisòkò's Son-Jara performance—are separate witnesses/continuities.

work_or_witnesses.work: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali
work_or_witnesses.edition: G. D. Pickett English translation; revised edition, 2006 (French original 1960); prose rendering framed as the words of Djeli Mamoudou Kouyaté

work_or_witnesses.work: John William Johnson, Son-Jara: The Mande Epic Performance by Jeli Fa-Digi Sisòkò
work_or_witnesses.edition: Indiana University Press, 2003; separate annotated Mandekan performance and English translation

coverage_rule: All principal named plot agents in the declared Niane/Pickett witness: royal family members who affect succession/exile, named jeliw and diviners/smiths who materially advise or act, named hunters, named rulers and commanders, and named supernatural/political antagonists. Unnamed offices and collective groups are excluded; genealogical forebears and named minor figures without material plot action are omitted.
omissions: The unnamed Hunter-Soothsayer of the opening prophecy, because this pass requires named character nodes.
Most genealogical ancestors, unnamed rulers, unnamed envoys, groups, and episodic warriors.
Characters, names, roles, and episodes found only in other oral performances, textualizations, adaptations, or modern reconstructions.
uncertainties: Niane's influential prose publication recasts oral material; chapter locators establish this witness only and do not establish a pan-Mande canonical version.
Spellings vary substantially across transliterations and performances (for example Sunjata/Sundiata/Son-Jara; Sumanguru/Soumaoro; Bala Faseke/Balla Fasséké).
Terms such as 'sorcerer,' 'prophet,' and 'griot' are English/French publication choices or comparative labels; source terms retain cautions and avoid treating them as fantasy classes.
evidence_basis: Claim-specific chapter locators in the declared published English witness, supplemented for scope and terminology by Indiana University's description of the distinct Fa-Digi Sisòkò performance and scholarly discussion of Sunjata variants and Mande kinship.

supports: Declared Niane/Pickett witness, its framing narrator, and chapter sequence.
A separately published full Mandekan text and English translation of Jeli Fa-Digi Sisòkò's performance; the epic remains widely recited.
